title: Kotta Pora
summary: Two players perch on a horizontal log held above a pit of soft mud or a pile of mats, one hand behind the back, and swing pillows at each other until one of them tips off. It is a game of laughter and quick balance, played at village gatherings.
howToPlay: Watch your rival's stance: it shows the swing that is coming.
Tap the answering move while the marker is in the bright zone.
Big swings push hard but arrive slowly; a quick tap lands first.
rules: Every swing, tap and brace beats two others and is beaten by two others.
A player pushed off the end of the log, or whose balance is gone, loses the round.
Timing sets the strength of a move: inside the bright zone is full strength.
A round also ends when one player is six points ahead or when the clock runs out.
Use Breathe to recover stamina; tired swings are weak.
heritageNote: Kotta pora is played in villages across Sri Lanka at the Sinhala and Tamil new year games, with a log set up over soft ground. Neighbours and cousins cheer, and the fall into the mud is part of the fun.
